rows.explainer: Seems like a real possibility, but would still give 70% chance that this process leads to at least a top charity. Main reason is Evidence Action's track record. I think in the 30% case we picked all the low hanging fruit: ie, the new programs just aren’t good enough. And the true probability for GIGs becoming top charities is 30% and only 3 make it to that stage, or something

rows.explainer: I haven't looked back at our GIG grants to think hard about what Phase 3 will cost, but my rough guess is that to get 1.5 top charities in expectation you'll need to scale 4 programs to phase 3 and spend $3m per program (including RCT costs). So, that's $12m in addition to the original $7.5m grant for Phases 1 and 2 to get 1.5 top charities

rows.explainer: GiveWell reports this model's result in multiples of cash transfers. Multiplying by GiveWell's value of a dollar to GiveDirectly converts it into units of value per dollar, so it ranks against the other models. Older sheets used older moral weights; the multiple of cash is the comparable number across years.
